why: This manifest exists because of a specific failure, not as ceremony.
The submission-integrity slice once shipped as its SQL migration ALONE:
rls/0022 created the live-intent indexes and the request ledger, and
nothing else landed — no ledger adapter, no request hashing, no HTTP
idempotency, no drizzle mirror, no proof. The table existed and was never
written to; the schema-drift gate was red for an unmirrored table; and the
front door still filed a second application for every retried POST.
A half-applied slice is worse than an unstarted one: the schema says the
guarantee is in place while the behaviour says otherwise.
Every artefact below is therefore asserted to exist, and to still contain
the symbol that makes it load-bearing, by
selfcheck/verify-submission-integrity.ts section 0 — which runs with no
infrastructure at all, so it is the first thing to go red.

artefacts.role: System of record: live-intent partial unique indexes + request ledger.
Both migrations run on every bootstrap, in the canonical order.
Readable mirror of the ledger table; keeps the drift gate green.
The mirror is exported, so drizzle-kit and consumers both see it.
Drizzle's belief about the post-bootstrap world includes the ledger.
Canonical, order-independent, length-prefixed request fingerprint.
The port: RECORDED / REPLAYED / KEY_REUSED / ALREADY_APPLIED.
PostgreSQL adapter: ledger + application + history + outbox in ONE tx.
One copy of the front-door INSERT, shared by both write paths.
The front door files through the ledger and surfaces its outcomes.
Idempotency-Key in, Idempotency-Replayed out, 409s for the refusals.
The ledger is actually WIRED — an adapter nobody constructs is dead code.
The on-site lane answers duplicates instead of faulting, and its write takes a StageEvents callback.
Classifies the live-intent refusal on the officer's write path, and stages the lane's events inside that same transaction.
409 ALREADY_APPLIED with the existing processing code for the tablet.
The unmodelled live-intent index is documented where a reader will look.
Same note for RNP.
Same note for RCS.
The proof runs in the quality gate — an unregistered proof never runs.

CI runs the same gate, so a regression cannot merge. The workflow invokes `pnpm verify`, which is scripts/run-selfchecks.sh (see the root package.json) — asserting on the command rather than the script path keeps this file out of the diff of every proof that is added.
The decision, its alternatives and what is deliberately NOT done.
How to run the proof and what each section establishes.

Grants the officer roles INSERT on the outbox so the walk-in write can stage its own events. Without it the staging call is a permission error and the lane silently reverts to announcing after commit.
Mints both envelopes BEFORE the write so the staged row and the dispatched object are one event, then dispatches post-commit through the outbox dispatcher rather than the bare bus.
Proves the application row and its outbox row share one transaction id, and that an injected staging failure rolls the entire write back.
